keyTakeaways: Live captions can help people follow important words together at weddings, conferences, classrooms and community events.
Audience members open Pockitle captions in a phone browser through a link or QR code; no dedicated audience app is required.
Each run uses one fixed spoken source language and can add up to three written translation languages.
Machine-generated captions support participation but do not replace professional CART, simultaneous interpreting or an official transcript.

faq.question: How do guests open Pockitle live captions?
faq.answer: They open an event link or scan its QR code in a phone browser. They do not need to install a dedicated audience app or create an audience account.

faq.question: Can Pockitle show captions in more than one language?
faq.answer: Yes. One run uses one fixed spoken source language, provides captions in that language, and can add up to three written translation languages.

faq.question: Can live captions help at weddings, conferences and in classrooms?
faq.answer: They can provide another reading route for guests, delegates and students who hear differently, process accents or technical terms, or prefer to read another language.

faq.question: Do Pockitle captions replace CART or professional interpreters?
faq.answer: No. Captions and translations are machine-generated and may be delayed, incomplete or wrong. They are not professional CART, simultaneous interpreting, an official transcript or a compliance guarantee.

glossary.definition: Text generated from speech and displayed while an event is happening.
The single fixed spoken language selected for one Pockitle run.
Automatically translated caption text offered in addition to the source-language captions.
The browser page that an audience member opens by link or QR code.
A professional real-time captioning service that Pockitle does not claim to replace.
